reason: Both conversations land on the acceptable conclusion - element most likely, control possible, engineer to test, no DIY part - and neither asks for the full model number. Conversation 2 gets there with clean, sensible questions (what is wrong, which zone, what hob type) and no missteps. Conversation 1 opens with child-lock and induction-pan speculation before knowing the hob type, then asks the homeowner to inspect the 'metal coil' or 'ceramic disc' under the rear right ring as if it were a solid-plate hob, which is impossible on a glass ceramic hob and forced the customer to correct it; it also misnames the control as a 'simmerstat' on a touch-control hob. Conversation 1 does add a useful 'stop using that zone' instruction, which narrows the gap, but Conversation 2 served the homeowner slightly better through accuracy and efficiency.
